failure_first_controls.control: Lexical prefix escape, naive symlink read, hardlink/FIFO replacement, descriptor-open fixture mutation, oversize content/closure, and stale expected hash are demonstrated/rejected.
Spawned-process races and reloads demonstrate one pending admission, retained uncertainty, and failure-closed stale lock for dev and one final-refit fence.
Fixture mutations, concurrent select/write, incorrect receipt/config, pending refit, duplicate lock, and tampered final-copy controls fail closed.
Changing a self-attested intent field changes the opened-byte closure while leaving solution byte hash unchanged.

implemented.descriptor_controls: O_NOFOLLOW descriptor reads; regular-file, single-link, size, dev/inode/mode/link/size/mtime/ctime pre/post checks; atomic same-directory O_EXCL temporary replacement with fsync.
implemented.dev_admission: Durable per-closure O_EXCL fence. PENDING is UNCERTAIN_NO_AUTOMATIC_RETRY equivalent; BOUND is not a retry permission. Distinct closures may be admitted before final selection.
implemented.final_lock: Requires a bound final-refit run id and matching task/environment/protocol hashes, reopens final code bytes, and binds code/closure/selection receipt/execution identity/manifests/run/artifact hashes.
implemented.final_refit: One campaign-wide typed final_refit fence requires FinalRefitPhase.FINAL_REFIT, the bound selection receipt, a frozen execution configuration hash, and separate outer-training and hidden-features manifest hashes. Hidden targets are not an input field. PENDING refuses automatic retry; root alone binds an externally observed run id.
implemented.final_selection: Requires a root-verified eligible development receipt tuple (receipt, closure, code), binds task/environment/protocol hashes, atomically copies opened solution bytes to private final-solution.py, then freezes source writes and later dev admission.
implemented.limits: TrustedIoLimits has required positive numerical caps with no defaults; file, closure, write, state, and name caps fail closed.
implemented.path_controls: Exact ASCII enum only; rejects absolute, traversal, NUL, Unicode/confusable, and all non-allowlisted names.
implemented.snapshots: Domain-separated closure SHA-256 derives from opened solution.py/research.md/intent.json bytes and length framing, not JSON self-attestation.
implemented.transaction_lock: One small O_EXCL transaction lock serializes cooperating mixed processes. A crash/stale lock is retained and returns LOCK_UNAVAILABLE; it is never silently removed.

integration_needed: Construct DevResultReceipt only after root verifies an actual permitted dev receipt; select_final_method requires its exact receipt SHA, closure SHA, and opened solution SHA.
Pass FinalSelectionBinding task/environment/protocol hashes at selection. Retain FinalSelection.selection_receipt_sha256 as a trusted root receipt reference.

Before final ORX launch, call admit_final_refit(FinalRefitIdentity(FINAL_REFIT,...)) with trusted immutable execution config, outer-training manifest, and hidden-features manifest hashes; on PENDING do not retry automatically. After external reconciliation call bind_final_refit(run_id).
Call lock_final_artifact only with the bound final run id and the same selection task/environment/protocol hashes. Root retains all ORX lifecycle and scientific authority.
limits_and_nonclaims: This is local at-most-once admission for cooperating processes, not external exactly-once ORX execution. Root must reconcile any PENDING admission with ORX before calling bind methods; this module never launches or retries ORX.
The trusted source/state roots and the trusted root bridge remain in the TCB. Same-UID hostile processes outside the cooperating lock protocol are not an OS sandbox threat model.
T01-T06, T08, T10-T13, and active extension source/loaded-path evidence in T16 are outside this owned module and were not executed here.
Dev aggregate exposure, container isolation, protected data custody, ORX receipt semantics, exact argv/image binding, and scorer sealing remain root/other-lane integration responsibilities.
